- When sentiment is negative and price is trending upward, model tends to overestimate — reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from recent peak), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +3–4% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model underreacts — increase forecast by 1–2% to capture sentiment momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements — apply a 1–2% upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model overcorrects downward — avoid sharp drops; maintain 0.5–1% above recent low.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast should not exceed it by more than 2% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses tail risk — add 0.5–1% buffer for volatility spikes in last 3–5 days if sentiment is volatile or negative.
